summary: In Greek mythology, Astydamea or Astydamia (Ancient Greek Ἀστυδάμεια) is a name attributed to several women. The atlas node astydamia-pelops is the daughter of Pelops and Hippodamia who marries Alcaeus and, in Apollodorus' primary account, bears Amphitryon and Anaxo — the Perseid queen through whom the Alcaeus line produces Heracles' foster-father.

sections.heading: Wife of Alcaeus
paragraphs: Apollodorus records that Alcaeus had Amphitryon and Anaxo by Astydamia daughter of Pelops, while noting rival mothers Laonome daughter of Guneus and Hipponome daughter of Menoeceus. Pausanias prefers Laonome — a disputed maternity beneath an undisputed Perseid line.

Homonym guard: not Astydamia wife of Acastus at Iolcus (astydamia-acastus); not Astydamia daughter of Amyntor (or Ormenus) among Heracles' lovers. The atlas id is the Pelopid mother of Amphitryon alone.
